trajectory.thought: The leader is a seeded baseline (median of full pool) and the verdict is 'indistinguishable' — the runner-up is not statistically better. The series has a strong trend with unstable model ranking and many correlated error groups, which is exactly the regime where a robust median of the full pool is the right combination: it captures the trend signal from the best models while being immune to any single model's idiosyncratic error. More turns are unlikely to turn this noise-level gap into a real gain.

action_args.justification: The series is trend-dominated (strength 0.96) with no seasonality and non-stationary. Model ranking is unstable (Kendall tau 0.228) and errors are heavily correlated (10 groups, only 4 independent), so no subset or fitted weighting can reliably outperform a robust full-pool median. The median naturally discards the influence of the worst-performing models while retaining the trend-capturing signal from the top catboost variants, and the 'indistinguishable' verdict confirms no other strategy is statistically superior.

   - All subset pools performed worse than the full pool median
   - The weighted approach (w1) was close but not better
